note: Establish a blend-oriented separation train with moderate operating intensity, then use the simulated purities and costs to refine it.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a six-column blend-oriented baseline: C4-/C5+, ethane/C3/C4, C5/C6+, C6 paraffins/heavies, and naphthenes/C7+. Then inspect purity and costs, prune low-value branches, and optimize the best cuts and operating settings.
Step 1 baseline simulation. Target products: C3, C4, C5, C6 paraffin and C6 naphthene blends; leave C7+ unsold initially. Moderate stages/reflux to control expensive-plant costs.

note: Prune the unprofitable train and test one sharp root split so downstream column sizes and cut quality can be designed from clean outlets.
notebook:
PLAN: First establish a sharp C4-/C5+ root split and measure cost. Then add C3/C4 and C5/C6+ splits, followed by C6-paraffin recovery only where product value exceeds cost. Prune all marginal branches.
Step 1: the 40-stage, reflux-2 baseline was much too sloppy and all six columns lost money. Root tops contained 12% C5 and no product met specification. Test a single much sharper root (70 stages, R=B=5); its outlet purity will determine economical downstream settings.

note: Reduce root severity and pressure, and add a tops column aimed directly at the high-value C5 blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a C5-/C6+ root, recover the valuable C5 blend from the tops, then test C4 recovery and C6-paraffin recovery only if each clears its column cost. Prune marginal branches.
Step 2: The 70-stage R=B=5 root actually cut C5-/C6+, but leaked 217 mol/s N-pentane into bottoms and cost $315M/yr. Reduce size/duty and pressure to cut refrigeration cost. Add a C4-/C5 split: its bottoms can earn roughly $600M/yr as C5 blend even without pure-component separation.

note: Sharpen the root at n-pentane/DMB and the tops column at n-butane/isopentane so the C5 blend reaches specification.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a C5-/C6+ root, recover the valuable C5 blend from the tops, then test C4 recovery and C6-paraffin recovery only if each clears its column cost. Prune marginal branches.
Step 2: Current 45/3 root cut isopentane rather than n-pentane and T split leaked butane badly. Increase both columns to 50-55 stages and R~5, targeting clean n-pentane/DMB and n-butane/isopentane cuts. C5 blend is worth about $614M/yr, so two effective columns can be profitable. Pressure drops 0.5/0.3 test cheaper operation while retaining separation.

note: Test strong, higher-pressure operation at both cuts to determine whether the two-column C5-blend route can reach saleable purity and positive margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a C5-/C6+ root, recover the valuable C5 blend from the tops, then test C4 recovery and C6-paraffin recovery only if each clears its column cost. Prune marginal branches.
Step 3: The moderate root and tops splits were not sharp: about half the n-pentane leaked to B and TB was only 61% C5. Test strong simultaneous reflux/boil-up at both cuts and higher pressure to learn whether the C5 blend can meet 95% and what the real cost ceiling is. If profitable, relax settings; if not, change the product sequence.

note: Use asymmetric root boil-up and tops reflux at lower pressure to recover n-pentane while rejecting n-butane from the C5 blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a C5-/C6+ root, recover the valuable C5 blend from the tops, then test C4 recovery and C6-paraffin recovery only if each clears its column cost. Prune marginal branches.
Step 3: At 60/8/8 the root lost substantial n-pentane to B and TB was only 76% C5 because n-butane leaked down. Test asymmetric operation: high root boil-up to recover C5, high tops reflux to reject C4, with lower pressure for easier separation. If TB reaches 95%, relax conditions; otherwise abandon the two-column C5 route.

note: Replace the failing indirect sequence with a direct C4-/C5+ split followed by a C5/C6+ split; this should make C4 rejection and C5 recovery much easier.
notebook:
PLAN: Switch to the direct sequence: first remove C4 and lighter overhead, then split the bottoms into a saleable C5 blend and C6+ residue. If C5 purity is adequate, reduce severity/cost; otherwise test one focused purity improvement. Later add C4 recovery only if profitable.
Step 1: The indirect C6+/C5- root caused n-pentane losses and excessive C4 in the final C5 stream, and extreme low-pressure settings failed. Use robust 50-stage columns: root n-butane/isopentane cut with high boil-up, then B isopentane/DMB cut. This should confine C4 leakage before the valuable C5 cut.

note: Correct both cut locations: sharply reduce root boil-up to retain C5 in the bottoms, and moderate the second cut to isolate C5 overhead at lower cost.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, B splits C5 blend from C6+. First obtain a saleable C5 stream, then reduce cost and consider C4 recovery. Step 1 correction: root boil-up 8 put essentially all C5 and some DMB overhead, so it was cutting at DMB/MCP rather than C4/C5. Lower root boil-up sharply to 1.5. B boil-up 10 on C6+ cut at hexane/MCP; use 5 to move its cut toward C5/C6. Reduce stages and operating intensity to control the very high costs.

note: Sharpen the C4/C5 root split with much higher reflux and lower boil-up, and move the second cut upward to isolate the C5 blend.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, B splits saleable C5 blend from C6+. Step 1: make the root C4/C5 cut sharp enough that residual n-butane cannot ruin BT purity, while moving B cut to C5/DMB. Then trim costs and consider C4 recovery. Learned: root 40/3/1.5 left about 270 mol/s n-butane in B; B 40/5/5 cut far too heavy and gave no products. Full pressure should improve relative volatility and avoid excessive pressure-drop cost.

note: Revert to the best valid design and use a moderate asymmetric root cut to reject butane overhead without the failed high-reflux operation; keep the C5/C6 split moderate for convergence.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, B splits saleable C5 blend from C6+. Step 1: obtain a converged sharp C4/C5 root cut with lower boil-up and moderate reflux, then tune B for 95% C5. Step 2: trim operating cost and consider C4 recovery. Learned: root 40/3/1.5 left about 270 mol/s n-butane in B; B 40/5/5 cut far too heavy and gave no products. Root 50/8/1 failed. Full or modestly reduced pressure should aid convergence and relative volatility; avoid extreme reflux.

note: Restore convergence with gentler full-pressure operation while retaining C5 in the root bottoms and taking C5 overhead in the second column.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, B splits saleable C5 blend from C6+. Step 1: obtain a converged sharp C4/C5 root cut with low boil-up and moderate reflux, then tune B for 95% C5. Step 2: trim operating cost and consider C4 recovery. Learned: root 40/3/1.5 left about 270 mol/s n-butane in B; B 40/5/5 cut far too heavy. Root 50/8/1 and 45/4/0.8 failed. Now use full pressure and gentler duties for convergence; avoid extreme reflux.

note: Simplify temporarily to one root column and use reduced pressure with moderate duties to restore convergence and reveal the actual C4/C5 split.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, then B splits C5 from C6+. Step 1: first obtain a converged one-column root cut at reduced pressure; inspect its component splits before restoring B. Step 2: add B only after a viable root is found, then trim costs and consider C4 recovery. Learned: root 40/3/1.5 converged but left about 270 mol/s n-butane in B; B 40/5/5 cut too heavy. Root 50/8/1 and 45/4/0.8 failed, as did full-pressure 40/3/0.5. Reduced pressure and moderate duties should improve convergence.

note: Raise root boil-up to move the cut from C3/C4 to C4/C5 while retaining moderate pressure and reflux for convergence.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, then B splits C5 from C6+. Step 1: tune a converged root to the C4/C5 boundary; inspect component splits before restoring B. Step 2: add B for C5 blend, then trim costs and consider C4 recovery. Learned: current 50/4/1 root cuts too light (376 mol/s tops), so boil-up must rise substantially. Earlier 40/3/1.5 also left much n-butane in B. Reduced-pressure moderate-duty columns converge best.

note: Sharpen the C4/C5 split by increasing boil-up and reflux enough to keep the C5 blend in the bottoms.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4 and lighter overhead, then B splits C5 from C6+. Step 1: tune a converged root to the C4/C5 boundary; inspect component splits before restoring B. Step 2: add B for C5 blend, then trim costs and consider C4 recovery. Current 45/3.5/2.5 sends all 864 mol/s C4- overhead plus about 80 mol/s C5; raise boil-up to 4 and reflux to 4 to push that C5 into B and sharpen the split. Reduced-pressure moderate-duty columns converge best.

note: Reduce root boil-up to retain the C5 components in the bottoms and move the overhead cut from C5/C6 back to the intended C4/C5 boundary.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4- overhead, then B splits C5 from C6+. Step 1: tune root to C4/C5; Step 2: add B for C5 blend; Step 3: recover C4 blend and trim costs. At 45/4/4/0.2, T=1260 versus C4-=864 and contains ~400 C5, so boil-up must be REDUCED, not raised. Try 45/4/2/0.2 to target ~864 tops while retaining convergence. Reduced-pressure moderate-duty columns have converged best.

note: Add a moderate reduced-pressure column on the root bottoms to take the C5 blend overhead while leaving the valuable C6+ material in the bottoms.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4- overhead, then B splits C5 from C6+. Step 1 root 45/4/2/0.2 gives T=761 and retains C5 in B; Step 2 add B for C5 blend; Step 3 recover C4 blend and trim costs. Root T remains C4 blend with ~103 mol/s light material in B, but B now has all C5. Try B at 40/3/2/0.2 to obtain C5 overhead; moderate reduced-pressure columns converge best. C5 blend potential about $179M/yr, so later stages must be reduced or additional valuable cuts recovered.

note: Push residual n-butane overhead at the root and retain C6+ in the second column bottoms, targeting a sellable C5 blend overhead.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4- overhead, then B isolates the valuable C5 blend. Current step: sharpen both cuts so BT reaches 95% C5. Root T=761 contains all C3/C4; at boil-up 2.0 about 100 mol/s n-butane leaked into B. Raise root boil-up to 2.5. B at 40/3/2/0.2 sent about 90 mol/s 2,2-DMB and other C6 into BT; reduce B boil-up to 1.2 to hold C6+ in BB. C5 blend revenue is roughly $610M/yr, enough to exceed the present $305M cost once purity is reached. After obtaining a valid sale, recover C4/C3 blends and/or trim column costs.

note: Increase both C5 recovery and C5/C6 sharpness in the second column; the present cut sacrifices too much C5 to the bottoms.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4- overhead, then B isolates the valuable C5 blend. Current step: sharpen B enough for BT to reach 95% C5. Root T=895 contains nearly all C3/C4; root B=2405 retains essentially all C5+. At B=40/3/1.2, BT=727 contains only about 465 mol/s C5 (64%), so boil-up 1.2 is too low despite low C6 contamination. Increase B to 60 stages, reflux 4 and boil-up 1.5 to recover more C5 while sharpening the C5/C6 boundary. C5 blend potential is about $620M/yr. Once sold, recover C4/C3 blends and/or trim root cost.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 boundary with more stages and reflux while reducing boil-up to limit C6 carryover into the C5 product.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4- overhead, then B isolates the valuable C5 blend. Current step: sharpen B enough for BT to reach 95% C5. Root T=895 contains nearly all C3/C4; root B=2405 retains essentially all C5+. At B=60/4/1.5, BT=710 has only ~510 C5 (72%) and ~190 C6; previous 40/3/1.2 was worse. Try fewer vapourised heavies (boil-up 1.0) with 80 stages and reflux 6, trading recovery for sharpness. C5 blend potential is about $620M/yr feed value; a partial high-purity cut can still sell. Once sold, recover C4/C3 blends and/or trim root cost.

note: Reduce heavy C6 carryover into the C5 cut, and add a C3/C4 splitter on the root tops to monetize both light blends.
notebook: PLAN: Direct sequence: root removes C4- overhead, B isolates C5 blend, and new T column separates C3 overhead from C4 bottoms. Current step: obtain the first sellable products. Root T=895 contains C3/C4 and only ~3% C5, so a C3/C4 split can yield two blends. At B=80/6/1.0, BT=426 was 87% C5 with 9% DMB and recovered only ~53% of feed C5. Reduce B boil-up to 0.65 to suppress DMB while retaining useful C5 recovery. T uses a moderate 40/3/1.2 cut. After revenue appears, optimize costs and recovery rather than separating C6+ components individually.
